guide.title: Setup guide
guide.subtitle: Create the OAuth application Sync needs, with the exact permissions it requests.

intro.google: Google Drive and the Workspace directory share one Cloud project: a few minutes in the console and one administrator decision.
intro.microsoft: One application registration in Microsoft Entra, one client secret and one tenant-wide admin consent.

warnings.api_enablement: Every API must be enabled in the same project as the OAuth client, otherwise the first directory call fails with a permission error.
warnings.consent_screen_type: An External consent screen still in testing mode only works for the accounts you published as test users, and its refresh tokens expire after seven days.
warnings.unverified_app: Google may require verification of the sensitive scopes; an unverified app is limited to a small number of users and shows a warning page.
warnings.admin_role_required: The account you connect must hold an administrator role: a permission granted to the application does not make the signed-in user an administrator.
warnings.license_required: The licence and role permissions only return data on a paid Google Workspace edition.
warnings.tenant_scope: Connect several directories with a multi-tenant app registration: keep the tenant id as common, every directory administrator consents once for their own directory, and the consent shown here is the one of the last directory that completed the flow.
warnings.work_accounts_only: Directory permissions cannot be granted to personal Microsoft accounts, so personal OneDrive accounts can no longer be connected.

project.title: Create or pick a Google Cloud project
project.body: Open the project list and create one (for example sync-files), or select the project this instance should use.

apis.title: Enable the three APIs
apis.body: Enable the Google Drive API, the Admin SDK API and the Enterprise License Manager API in that project. A directory permission fails until the API it belongs to is enabled.

consent.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen
consent.body: Choose Internal for a Workspace domain (no Google verification), or External with your accounts published as test users. Add the permissions Sync requests; Google classifies the admin.directory.* ones as sensitive.

client.title: Create the OAuth client
client.body: Credentials > Create credentials > OAuth client ID > Web application. Copy the client id and the client secret into the credentials of this instance.

redirect.title: Add the authorised redirect URI
redirect.body: In the same client, add the URL below to the authorised redirect URIs and save. A missing or extra character here is the most common registration failure.

permissions.title: Add the requested permissions
permissions.body: Paste the list below where the consent screen asks for scopes. Sync requests them all at once, so a connection made today stays valid after an upgrade.

admin.title: Allow the app in the Admin console
admin.body: In Security > API controls > App access control, mark the client ID as trusted (or add it to the allow-list of your organisational units).

connect.title: Connect an administrator account
connect.body: Connect a Workspace administrator (a super administrator for the directory permissions). Sync acts as that account, so revoke its consent when you stop using the instance.

app.title: Register an application
app.body: In Microsoft Entra (Applications > App registrations) create a registration, for example Sync. Choose Accounts in this organizational directory only to serve one directory, or Accounts in any organizational directory (multi-tenant) to let several directories connect to the same app: each one grants the consent with its own administrator.

redirect.title: Add the redirect URI
redirect.body: Authentication > Add a platform > Web, then paste the URL below. Leave the implicit grant options off: Sync uses the authorization code flow with PKCE.

secret.title: Create a client secret
secret.body: Certificates & secrets > New client secret, copy the value immediately and store it in the credentials of this instance. Note the expiry date: an expired secret breaks every job.

permissions.title: Add the Microsoft Graph permissions
permissions.body: API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > Delegated permissions, then add every permission of the list below. All of them need an administrator to consent.

consent.title: Grant the admin consent
consent.body: A tenant administrator grants the permissions once for the whole directory. With a multi-tenant registration open this page from each directory that has to connect: the consent is granted per directory and the button below belongs to the directory of the signed-in administrator.

role.title: Check the administrator role
role.body: Consent is not a privilege: the identity that connects must also hold a directory role (User Administrator, Groups Administrator or License Administrator) to perform an operation.

connect.title: Connect the account
connect.body: Connect the account from the accounts screen. Reconnecting it later is what applies a permission a future version adds.
